Thanks Ben  that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side while we wait for legal: 

- Controller vs Processor: Oakridge will be the controller; any obligations Redwood has as a processor should be spelled out (purpose limitation, documented instructions).
- Subprocessors: We need a current list of subprocessors and at least 30 days notice of any additions. Can you confirm how often that list is updated?
- Breach notice: Our policy requires notification of suspected or confirmed data breaches affecting Oakridge data within 48 hours of detection, plus written follow-up with root cause and mitigation plan. Does Redwood have a policy SLA that fits this window?
- Retention/Deletion: We need the ability to configure retention per dataset and a documented deletion process (including proof of deletion on request).

Also, two items from procurement: any standard indemnity caps or required cyber insurance limits? Michael will follow up separately on procurement/insurance.

Appreciate the quick turnaround  if Marissa can propose the exact DPA language that addresses the three bullets above, we can route through our procurement next week.

Hi Sarah / Ben,

Thanks for the context and the redlines. Below is a concise legal response to Oakridge's items  happy to expand or hop on a call to go line-by-line.

1) Controller / Processor
- Confirmation: Redwood Inference will process customer content as a processor on behalf of Oakridge Health (controller) for the purposes described in the DPA and underlying MSA. We will act only on documented instructions from Oakridge, except as required by law. Suggested contract language provided in the attached memo.

2) Subprocessors
- Current list: We maintain a current list of subprocessors at https://www.redwood.ai/subprocessors (note: this is updated quarterly and whenever a new critical subprocessor is added).
- Notice: Redwood will provide 30 days' notice of new subprocessors where feasible; for urgent security-related additions we will notify as soon as practicable and provide opt-out controls (e.g., right to object to specific subprocessor use).

3) Breach notification
- Our standard incident response process: we will notify customers of confirmed incidents involving customer data within 48 hours of detection of a confirmed security incident affecting customer data, followed by timely written updates with remediation steps and root-cause analysis. We can include the 48-hour notification SLA in the DPA.

4) Retention and deletion
- Redwood supports customer-configurable retention policies per dataset. We provide a documented deletion workflow and can furnish confirmation of deletion (audit log + deletion job id) on request. For regulated workloads requiring shorter retention windows, we can accommodate contractual retention periods and deletion proof.

5) Insurance / Indemnity
- Standard: Redwood carries a cyber insurance policy with $5M limit and accepts industry-standard indemnity language. If Oakridge requires higher limits, we can evaluate but may need approval from finance/executive team.

Attachments included: SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf (summary of controls) and a short legal memo with suggested DPA language (summary pasted into the attachment stub).

Proposed next steps:
- I will circulate a redlined DPA with the controller/processor clause, subprocessors clause, explicit 30-day notice and 48-hour breach notification SLA.
- If Oakridge is comfortable, we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call Thurs or Fri to finalize language.

Please let me know which time works best.

Best,
